correctness.rationale: For connected unweighted finite simple G on N>=3, P_h=2(I+hL_G/2)^(-1)-I, and the inverse of the irreducible M-matrix has positive off-diagonals. Since L_KN-L_G is a positive semidefinite complement Laplacian, inverse Loewner order gives C_G,ii >=(1+t)/(1+Nt), t=h/2. The equality criterion for a positive-semidefinite inverse difference reduces to (L_KN-L_G)e_i=0, equivalent to i being universal. It follows that h<=2/(N-2) is nonnegative on every graph, with exactly universal vertices having vanishing holding entries at the boundary. The block Schur complement at a universal vertex gives (P_h)_vv=(2-(N-2)h)/(2+Nh), negative immediately beyond the boundary. The connected two-vertex exception remains positive for all finite h. Independently enumerated all 770 connected labeled simple graphs on N=3..5, confirming exact equality support on all of them (283 graphs with at least one universal vertex); finite checks corroborate, do not establish the universal proof.

evidence: Reversible Markov-chain theory covers the same Crank–Nicolson positivity operator on each fixed graph. The heat-equation Dirichlet-grid paper is for a mesh family with boundary conditions, not connected graph order extremizers.

value.rationale: Uniform positivity timesteps are natural stability limits for diffusion on graphs. This settles the exact worst-case threshold over all connected simple graphs of each order and uniquely characterizes extremal graph structure and zero-return sites, rather than restating the prior fixed-chain resolvent test.

limitations: Connected unweighted simple graphs N>=3 and exceptional N=2. Positivity of one full Crank–Nicolson update only, not stage positivity or higher-order error. Individual thresholds for graphs without universal vertices are not explicitly computed.
